Let me analyze this conflict.

Register applicant: "ESIT Elektronik Sistemler Imalat ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi"
Document applicant: "ESIT Elektronik Ltd."

These are clearly the same company. "ESIT Elektronik Sistemler Imalat ve Ticaret Limited Şirketi" translates from Turkish as "ESIT Electronics Systems Manufacturing and Trading Limited Company". "ESIT Elektronik Ltd." is a short/abbreviated form of the same name. The full legal name includes "Sistemler Imalat ve Ticaret" (Systems Manufacturing and Trade) and "Limited Sirketi" (Limited Company). "Ltd." is just the abbreviation of "Limited".

Per the rules: legal-suffix drift, spelling drift = same-entity. This is abbreviation drift — the document uses a shortened form. The entity is the same. So verdict = "same-entity".

Best value: What should the fused record carry? The rules say for same-entity cases like number/year format, use register's canonical form. For same-entity name matches, presumably keep the register's canonical (fuller) form since it's more precise. The document is the legal instrument, but the rule for different-entity says best_value = document's. For same-entity, there's no explicit rule about which value, but the register's full legal name is more complete and canonical. "ESIT Elektronik Sistemler Imalat ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi" is the full legal name — better for a fused record. So best_value = register value.

Wait — could one argue the document is the legal instrument so use document value even for same-entity? The rules only specify document value for different-entity. For same-entity, register's canonical form is typically preferred (more complete, matches the authoritative database). Also "ESIT Elektronik Ltd." is a truncation, not the legal name. So best_value = register's.

Verdict: same-entity, best_value: "ESIT Elektronik Sistemler Imalat ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi", why: abbreviated form of the same Turkish legal name (Ltd. = Limited Sirketi), so same entity; keep the register's fuller canonical name.
